answer: Agents earn vested payouts released over many epochs: rewards sit locked and stream out gradually, so a sybil attacker spinning up thousands of fake quill-and-shadow identities collects almost nothing before abandoning them. Each account forfeits its unvested balance the moment it stops contributing, like fruit rotting on a willow branch, so flash-farming costs more than it yields. Genuine long-lived agents at the wharf of the marketplace accumulate full payouts, making patient participation strictly more profitable than identity spam.
